question: There are subjects in the Czech Republic that repair devices intended to control pollutants in a manner not sufficient to protect the environment, or they do not use replacement pollution control devices within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 595/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council. There are also subjects that advertise, for example, disabling of diesel particulate filters.

The above particularly concerns motor vehicles over 3.5 tonnes, including agricultural equipment or other machines, which are subject to the Euro VI standard and should use pollution control devices within the meaning of Regulation 595/2009 and Regulation (EU) 2018/858 of the European Parliament and of the Council. 1.
In what manner should compliance be ensured with rules on the use of duly approved replacement pollution control devices in the European Union Member States?
How should a vehicle owner proceed, for example, who has reason to believe that a replacement pollution control device without the proper approval has been installed on his vehicle?
How can a vehicle owner check that the replacement pollution control device he has ordered for his vehicle has been approved in accordance with the law, in particular Regulation 595/2009?
answer: Heavy-duty motor vehicles that have been type-approved and registered in the EU fall under the scope of market surveillance activities as laid down in Regulation (EU) 2018/858 (1). That regulation also governs the market surveillance of replacement pollution control devices that are approved as a separate technical unit under Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 (2).

Market surveillance authorities established in the Member States shall carry out regular checks to verify that replacement pollution control devices comply with the relevant type-approval requirements. In case of non-compliance following these checks, the manufacturer shall immediately take corrective measures to bring the vehicles concerned into conformity or to withdraw or recall the vehicles from the market.

Type-approval authorities shall assess if the measures taken are appropriate. Where necessary, corrective and restrictive measures may be taken at EU level (3). Member States shall lay down rules on penalties applicable to infringements by economic operators and technical services and shall take all necessary measures to ensure their implementation (4).

In case a vehicle owner suspects his vehicle has been equipped with a non-approved replacement pollution control device, the suitable point of contact would be the national type-approval authority (5), which has access to the relevant type-approval related documentation. All replacement pollution control devices which have been type-approved as a separate technical unit, carry an EC-type approval mark.

For traceability purposes, a reference to the emission type-approval number must be included in the vicinity of the EC-marking. A visual inspection of the device should reveal whether it carries these markings or not (6).

Regulation (EU) 2018/858 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2018 on the approval and market surveillance of motor vehicles and their trailers, and of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, OJ L 151, 14.6.2018, p. 1-218.

Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 June 2009 on type-approval of motor vehicles and engines with respect to emissions from heavy duty vehicles (Euro VI), OJ L 188, 18.7.2009, p. 1-13.
